title: Mobile service ownership and composition
approved_scope: Compose App.tsx as AuthProvider -> P2PProvider -> RootNavigator and retain the explicit P0 diagnostic oracle.
Add one inert, framework-independent BareRuntimeClient -> P2PService boundary with typed lifecycle errors and subscribable snapshots.
Modify only the ten frozen source/test paths and P1.F2 evidence/status artifacts listed by the approved card.
excluded_scope: P0 source deletion, Hyperdrive, Corestore, Hyperswarm, discovery, networking, fixture storage, product API/UI, backend, HTTP/HLS, persistence/identity, and iOS.
Commits, pushes, deployment, or any external write.
acceptance: HP-F2: App.tsx composes AuthProvider -> P2PProvider -> RootNavigator, and the explicit P0 diagnostic calls initialize -> ping -> shutdown through the stable service boundary.
EC-F2: mounting, rerendering, navigation, and auth-route changes do not auto-start, duplicate, or leak a runtime; invalid lifecycle calls remain typed.

RootNavigator creates neither auth nor P2P provider; normal mounting is network-inert; focused P0/client/service/provider tests, typecheck, lint, full Jest, three Reflection passes, coverage certification, owner verification, and status synchronization pass.
constraints: P2PProvider owns one stable P2PService; P2PService owns one product BareRuntimeClient; neither service nor navigator depends on React routes.
Use an external-store subscription boundary for status consumers; do not start network activity merely because the provider mounts.
Keep the P0 source in place as a characterization oracle until separately gated P1.F3a; proof commands may not enter the product service API.
Stop and return to scoring/review/approval if any edit or behavior escapes the frozen P1.F2 boundary.
